clue.text: Set meal and free bed at hotel

indicators.note: free here means loosed from its order, so the three words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hotel offers a fixed-price dinner plus a complimentary bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' signals the anagram: the letters of BED AT HOTEL are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed menu at a set price is the French-named restaurant option.

clue.text: Lift elbow to highest point

parts.note: raising the elbow as high as it goes is the drinker draining a glass, so the clue paints heavy drinking

explanation.definitionFit: To drink alcohol habitually and to excess, the bent arm raised high.

clue.text: College accounts cause fights for the auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: battles are fights

explanation.surface: University accountants provoke quarrels with the auditors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' suggests accountants, fitting 'accounts'; here they are listeners. At Oxford college bills for board and lodging have this name.
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford, the term for a student's termly bill from the college for food and lodging.

clue.text: It's terribly noisy in the grain division

parts.note: an ear is the grain-bearing head of a cereal plant
splitting is dividing

explanation.surface: A threshing floor is a deafening place.
explanation.definitionFit: So loud it seems to hurt the hearing.

clue.text: Hire mixing machine for the family treasure

indicators.note: mixing tells us to jumble the letters of the word before it

parts.note: a loom is a weaving machine

explanation.surface: Rent a blender to look after the precious family possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A valued object handed down through generations.

clue.text: Miniature enthrals Welsh maid

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so the first word holds the other inside

parts.note: teeny means tiny

explanation.surface: A tiny portrait captivates a girl from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: A tweeny was a young servant girl working between cook and housemaid in Victorian households.
explanation.definitionFit: A between-maid, the junior servant assisting both kitchen and housemaids.

clue.text: Sea captain who married a Jezebel

explanation.surface: A skipper's unwise choice of a scheming wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Two people share the name: Melville's whaling captain in Moby-Dick, and the Old Testament king of Israel whose wife was Jezebel.
explanation.definitionFit: One name covers the obsessive whaler of Moby-Dick and the biblical king wedded to the wicked queen.

clue.text: Henry King once got behind a rocky ridge

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Og was the giant king of Bashan in the Old Testament
back means behind

explanation.surface: A king of old takes cover behind a craggy ridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry King' looks like a single monarch; it is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep-sided crest of hill shaped like a pig's spine.

clue.text: Gloomy Uriah admits son is family scoundrel

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed within the others

parts.note: black means gloomy
Uriah Heep is the scheming clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A melancholy Uriah confesses that his boy is the disgrace of the family.
explanation.definitionFit: The disreputable member a family is ashamed of.

clue.text: Safe blower who started series of small explosions

definitions.text: who started series of small explosions

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
a piper blows into his instrument

explanation.surface: A safecracker who set off a run of small blasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe blower' suggests a safecracker; it is two pieces. The tongue-twister 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers' is a string of little popping P sounds, explosive consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursery tongue-twister's opening name launches a run of plosive P consonants.

clue.text: Once a capital silver artist

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A silversmith who used to work in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city was the seat of the Mughal emperors before the court moved to Delhi.

clue.text: Additional racehorses in reserve

parts.note: second means another, an additional one
a string is the stable of racehorses kept by one owner or trainer

explanation.surface: Spare racehorses kept back for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Backup or reserve, as a substitute team or player.

clue.text: Tom's furtive look

parts.note: His glance is the brief secret one he gave

explanation.definitionFit: A quick sly glance is what gave Coventry's Peeping Tom his name.

clue.text: NCO cut an honour

parts.note: to lance is to cut open, as a boil
in bridge the jack is one of the honour cards

explanation.surface: A non-commissioned officer is stripped of a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'honour' suggests a medal; in card games such as bridge the honours are the top cards, ace to ten, so the jack is one. A lance-jack is British army slang for a lance corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: Army slang for a lance corporal, the lowest non-commissioned rank.

clue.text: School's first head girl is a hare-brained child

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: a cape or headland juts into the sea
Grace is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The school's first head girl is a scatterbrain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head girl' reads as a prefect; split, 'head' is a promontory and 'girl' a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, good-for-nothing young rogue.

clue.text: Found goose very unyielding

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
a tailor's goose is a heavy smoothing iron

explanation.surface: A goose discovered to be extremely stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' is not the past of find but the verb to found, as in a foundry; and the goose is a tailor's pressing iron, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal poured into moulds is rigid and brittle, so the phrase describes anything inflexible.

clue.text: Sound rugby forward is a smoker

indicators.note: Sound tells us to take the word as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the hooker is the front-row forward who hooks the ball in the scrum

explanation.surface: A healthy rugby forward turns out to be a smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'healthy' but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A water pipe is something people draw tobacco through, so it is a device for smoking.

clue.text: H. Finn's contribution to the overdrafts manager

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Huckleberry Finn's donation to a bank's lending officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Huckleberry Finn floats down the Mississippi on a raft, so he is one who travels by raft.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boy hero drifts downriver on a raft, making him a raft-rider.

clue.text: Range of colours, say, shows a sense of taste

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the word, giving one that is pronounced the same

parts.note: an artist's palette is the range of colours used

explanation.surface: A painter's choice of colours reveals their discerning taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof of the mouth is figuratively one's ability to discriminate flavours.

clue.text: A feline poet who repels one

indicators.note: repels means drives away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Giacomo Leopardi was an Italian poet
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A catlike poet who drives off a single admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spotted big cat.

clue.text: Simple spread — wild duck?

parts.note: bald means plain or simple, as in a bald statement
pâté is a paste spread on toast

explanation.surface: A plain spread — is it made from wild duck?
explanation.walkthrough: The duck is the American wigeon, so called from the white patch on its crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The American wigeon is known by this name for its white crown patch.

clue.text: The. representative of justice tears off among the motorists

indicators.note: among puts the one inside the other

parts.note: the AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring organisation

indicators.note: off means awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Justice's representative weeps among the drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' signals the anagram of TEARS (STRAE), and 'among' puts it inside AA. Astraea is the Greek goddess of justice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek star-maiden who personified justice and left the earth last.

clue.text: What is needed is no huge change

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: What's required is not a massive overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufficient, as much as required.

clue.text: Disastrous scheme to drug nun's. stew

indicators.note: stew as an instruction to cook the letters together, mixing them up

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful plan to sedate a nun's casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' signals rearranging TO DRUG NUN. The postwar British Groundnut Scheme to grow peanuts in Tanganyika was a famously costly failure.
explanation.definitionFit: The postwar peanut-growing project in East Africa became a byword for a costly government fiasco.

clue.text: Sums — little ones

explanation.surface: Arithmetic for small children.
explanation.definitionFit: Adds up figures as a verb, and small children as a noun.

clue.text: Oh, it's incredible!

parts.note: a sarcastic exclamation of disbelief, as in a scornful 'oh, sure'

explanation.definitionFit: Said sarcastically, an informal yes expresses disbelief.

clue.text: Just open for a drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A pub just opening its doors for a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open, not quite shut.

clue.text: Two people to an office in Rome

definitions.text: Two people to an office in Rome

parts.words: Two people to an office in Rome
parts.note: in ancient Rome some magistracies were held jointly by a pair of officials, and the word names that joint post

explanation.definitionFit: A Latin-derived term for government shared by a pair of officials, as in Roman magistracies.

clue.text: Boy in a whirl

explanation.surface: A lad spinning round in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A male name, and a swirling circular current of water or air.

clue.text: Service chart marker

parts.note: a tea or dinner service is a set of china
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A diagram used in the forces or by the post office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests the armed forces; it is crockery. The answer is a wax pencil for writing on glass or china.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax pencil used to write on glazed surfaces.
